title: Stabilizer Evaluation Map Calculation
body_html:
Stabilizer Evaluation Map Calculation

For the one-block stabilizer \(S\), evaluation at \(1\) gives an isomorphism \[ \operatorname{Ind}_S^{S K_{M,+}}\omega_w[\chi_M|_{K_{M,+}}] \simeq S(b)^{b_C}. \] Under \(S(b)^{b_C}\simeq S(b_0)\), the translated \(S K_{M,+}\)-action is:

  • elements in the positive-depth \(\Delta^j K_{M,+}\)-factors act by the character \(\chi_M\);
  • elements of \(G_{x,s}\times G'_{x',s}\) act by \(\chi_M\) times the Heisenberg operator attached to their image in \(b_0\);
  • \(\Delta^0\) acts through the residual Weil representation on \(b_0\).

Consequently, \[ \operatorname{Ind}_S^{\Delta^0K_{M,0+}}\omega_w[\chi_M|_{K_{M,+}}] \simeq \kappa_M|_{\Delta^0K_{M,0+}}. \]
proof_html: Frobenius reciprocity reduces the evaluation map to the \(\chi_M\)-isotypic component for \(S\cap K_{M,+}\). Lemma 7.3 gives the action of each stabilizer factor. The \(G_{x,s}\times G'_{x',s}\) factors generate the isotropic subspace \(b_C\), so the isotypic component is exactly \(S(b)^{b_C}\). Gérardin's mixed model identifies this invariant space with \(S(b_0)\), and Lemma 6.10 removes the determinant character on \(\Delta^0\). Lemma 7.5 supplies the final one-dimensional Hom calculation against \(\kappa_M\), giving the induced-module isomorphism.

deps.title: Isotypic Components Commute with Compact Induction
